lines.text: What if I told you any drawing can be made with nothing but spinning circles?
This letter is drawn by forty-five of them.
Let's take it one piece at a time.
A point going around a circle.
Keep only its up-and-down motion, and what comes out is a wave.
Now hook another circle onto its tip: three times smaller, and spinning three times faster.
The wave isn't so smooth anymore.
Keep adding circles, each one smaller and faster, and something strange happens.
Out of pure spinning, you get sharp corners.
Any signal can be built as a sum of circles.
And if you let the tip move freely on the plane, instead of keeping just one direction, you're back to the drawing from the start.
None of these circles knows it's drawing.
Each one just spins at its own pace.
Keep only the big circles, and you're left with a rough version of the drawing.
That's exactly the idea behind how a JPEG shrinks a photo, and an MP3 shrinks a song.
They keep the big circles, and throw away the tiny ones you'd never notice.
